Chairman of the Advocacy for Nigeria Football Reform Initiative, Harrison Jalla, has rejected the appointment of Sampson Ebomhe as chairman of FIFA’s newly constituted Nigeria Football Federation Normalisation Committee, citing alleged conflict of interest and lack of neutrality, The PUNCH reports. Jalla, in a statement on Thursday, questioned FIFA’s background checks on Ebomhe and said his organisation would submit details of its objections to the world football governing body. FIFA on Wednesday announced the five-member committee, with Ebomhe named as chairman alongside governance expert Dr Joe Abah, veteran sports journalist and administrator Godwin Enakhena, Amina Yerima and former Super Eagles player Daniel Amokachi. “The Advocacy for Nigeria Football Reform Initiative rejects the FIFA Normalisation Committee Chairman, Mr Sampson Ebomhe, whose appointment was announced in a list released on November 18, 2026, on the grounds of conflict of interest and lack of neutrality. “FIFA certainly has not conducted a proper background check on the purported chairman of the Normalisation Committee. Details of our objection and verifiable facts will be filed with FIFA immediately,” he said. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources The committee is expected to oversee the affairs of the NFF alongside its secretariat, review the federation’s statutes and organise fresh elections to usher in a new leadership. FIFA unveils presidential candidates to challenge Infantino’s re-election Ecuadorian footballer banned for eight years after throwing stone at referee Infantino faces fresh questions over FIFA term limit Its mandate runs until May 31, 2027, at the latest, with the members’ confirmation subject to eligibility checks by FIFA’s Review Committee. Meanwhile, UK-based Nigerian journalist Osasu Obayiuwana has questioned the duration of the committee’s mandate, arguing that the period may not be sufficient to carry out meaningful reforms in Nigerian football administration. “If FIFA really wants to help football in Nigeria to be in a better place, the NFF Normalisation Committee should have a minimum one-year mandate to do a thorough rebuild. A six-month mandate will solve nothing,” Obayiuwana said. FIFA’s intervention followed the resignation of NFF president Ibrahim Gusau, General Secretary Mohammed Sanusi and members of the federation’s executive committee on August 27, 2026, which disrupted preparations for the federation’s elective congress scheduled for September 27. Ebomhe previously chaired the NFF Electoral Committee that conducted the federation’s executive committee elections in Warri, Delta State, in 2014. He was also appointed vice-chairman of the National Sports Commission’s seven-member electoral committee for national sports federation elections in August 2025.
